consensus_findings.description: Critical: D1 and task 3.1 require JSON Schema, OpenAPI, Python, and TypeScript to accept the same context objects, but the structural schemas and generated TypeScript still admit objects that Python rejects. Draft-2020-12 validation accepts a traceparent whose embedded IDs differ from trace_id/span_id (and an attempt_number unrelated to claim_generation), while the Pydantic model rejects it; the TypeScript aliases are plain string and an entirely invalid OperationContextEnvelope compiles without invoking any guard.

Critical: the SQL null-bypass is not fully closed. A non-null submission_context can contain JSON null for traceparent, trace_id, and span_id while the duplicated columns are SQL NULL; key-presence and size checks pass, every nullable column check passes, and IS NOT DISTINCT FROM considers each null pair equal. This contradicts the non-null envelope schema and the iteration-4 claim that every duplicate is required when canonical context exists.

Nit: the TypeScript signed-BIGINT guard tests an unbounded decimal regex and then constructs BigInt(value) before checking the 19-character contract limit, so a long digit string reaches an unnecessarily expensive arbitrary-precision parse even though every canonical value is at most 19 characters.

The revision correctly adds executable process-health lifecycle columns and exact expiry constraints, explicit claim-generation headroom, null-safe duplicate comparisons, bounded Python scalars, non-zero W3C identifiers, and a still-valid package DAG.
